Learning Loving Living
Home
Our school is a family... We educate, encourage and support each child to realise his or her potential within a Christian setting.
Welcome to All Saints' and St Richard’s Church of England Primary School.
We are a small school based in the rural village of Old Heathfield.The Victorian listed frontage of the building screens the modern, spacious classrooms that sit behind this; a lovely mix of old and new.
We pride ourselves on getting to know each child as an individual therefore strengths are built upon and areas of development are supported. We make the most of our beautiful setting with weekly Forest School sessions.
At ASSR we believe that children thrive in an environment in which they are happy, challenged and secure. We aim to provide the best primary education in a stimulating and creative environment so that every child realises their potential.

pageCache.text:
Wraparound and After School Clubs
Wraparound in Partnership With CATS Club
CATS Club provide our wraparound care from 7:30 to 18:00.
Breakfast Clubs open at 7:30, children are warmly welcomed and registered by the friendly CATS Club staff.
A healthy breakfast is served until 8:10, with children able to choose from a selection of cereals, fruit or toast with a variety of toppings.
After breakfast, children have time to socialise with friends or take part in a range of quiet table-top activities. Breakfast club has a calm atmosphere which helps the children to start their day positively and feel prepared for a successful day of learning when they enter their classroom.
Our caring and supportive environment encourages children to develop confidence, independence, and positive friendships while enjoying a safe and enjoyable start to their school day.
Please use the following link to book.
To make bookings, you will need to create a customer account with EEQU. Once your account has been set up, you will be able to book and pay for all Breakfast Club, Afterschool Club and Holiday Playscheme sessions online.
After school there are plenty of activities on offer and lots of space for the children, with full use of the school's facilities and incredible outdoor space. Arts & craft, lego, and sporting activities are some of the children's favourites.
The different sessions on offer enable flexibility for our families, and the opportunity to combine wraparound with other afterschool clubs.
A short session runs from 15:20 to 16:30 and includes a drink and snack.
A full session runs from 15:20 to 18:00 and includes drinks, snacks and a cooked tea.
A half session runs from 16:30 to 18:00 and includes a cooked tea.
Ofsted registration means that families are able to use Tax Free Childcare to help pay for the provision. The afternoon Short, half and full sessions enable flexibility for families.
For registration forms, or for any enquiries, please email catsafterschool@aol.com or call 07484 300707.
Our wraparound welcomes children from all local Heathfield primary schools, with collection from their school by CATS staff included at no extra cost.

Admissions
Joining Reception
If your child is due to start primary school in September 2026, you must apply for a school place via East Sussex County Council’s website. The closing date for applications for September 2026 intake is 15 January 2026 . National offer day for primary school places is 16 April 2026. Please visit the County Council website for further details on school admissions.
East Sussex County Council's website has lots of information to help parents and carers who are applying for their child's school place.
Starting school for the first time
Starting school is an important milestone in every child’s life and at ASSR we are passionate about making the transition to school a positive one for every pupil.
All children starting school in Reception will receive a home visit from the Reception Class Teacher and Teaching Assistant. This gives us the opportunity to speak to our new families and see the children in a setting where they are most comfortable.
Following the nursery visit all parents and carers are invited to a meeting at ASSR to discuss the arrangements for starting school and parents have the opportunity to ask questions.
The children are then invited to come and spend a session in school getting to know their new surroundings.
Our new reception starters are allocated buddies from Year 6 who will help them to settle in from September. The buddies will write a letter to their Reception Pupil with a photo attached.
Finally in September, just before the children start school, the class teacher visits the children at home.
In year admissions
An in-year admission is the admission of a pupil to a school which takes place outside of the normal entry times. We recommend parents and carers apply online at the East Sussex County Council site, following the link below.
In year admissions arrangements
Please contact our School Secretary, Mrs Cuming if you have any questions about admissions office@assr.e-sussex.sch.uk

PE
We are proud to have achieved the School Games Mark Gold Award for the third year in a row!
At ASSR our aim is to ensure that all children are engaged in, enjoy and understand the value and importance of physical education for both mental and physical health. We strive to achieve this through quality teaching of the subject, allowing our children access to a range of equipment, sports teaching and cross-curricular activities encouraging inclusivity for all age ranges, abilities and needs.
Across Key Stage 1, teachers instil knowledge of team games, basic movement, such as running, jumping, skipping, and introduce the art of performance through dance and gymnastics. These skills are vital for the physical development of our youngsters as they grow and progress into Key Stage 2.
Over Key Stage 2, the children partake in the learning of more complex and in-depth skills, such as playing competitive games and understanding the basic principles of attacking and defending. This, as well as performance through dance, to develop flexibility and strength, and taking part in outdoor activities, enables our children to develop into experienced sportsmen and women. With the wide range of activities, sports and equipment the children have access to at ASSR, our mission is to give them strategies to manage both their physical and mental health and the demands of everyday life. We strive to develop our children’s personalities through sport, with the hope that, as they grow, they will thrive and develop a lifelong passion for physical education.
We proudly encourage healthy living at ASSR and we are an active member of the Heathfield School Sports Partnership.

RE
Curriculum intent statement
At All Saints' and St Richard's CE Primary we strive to provide an environment where pupils are able to explore challenging questions about the ultimate meaning and purpose of life, beliefs about God, themselves and the nature of reality, issues of right and wrong and what it means to be human.
Through developing the pupils’ knowledge and understanding of Christianity, and principal religions, religious traditions and other world religions they explore views that offer answers to these big questions. The RE Curriculum provides opportunities for personal reflection and spiritual development alongside enhancing pupils’ awareness and understanding of religions and beliefs, teachings and practices and looks the influence of religion on individuals, families, communities and cultures.
Pupils develop their sense of identity and belonging enabling them to flourish individually within their communities and as citizens in a pluralistic society and within a global community. Religious Education has an important role in preparing pupils for adult life, employment and lifelong learning.
At ASSR we use the East Sussex agreed syllabus for teaching principle world religions across EYFS, KS1 and KS2.
We use the Understanding Christianity programme for the Christianity units taught in every year group.
https://www.understandingchristianity.org.uk/

RSHE
Curriculum intent statement
Our school’s overarching aims and objectives for pupils are for children to ‘live life to the full’, inline with the Church of England’s Vision for Education. RSHE is underpinned by a clear set of embedded values and principles that complement the school ethos and permeate through the teaching practice, resources and classroom management of RSHE lessons.
RSHE is learning about the emotional, social and physical aspects of growing up, relationships, sex, human sexuality and sexual health in an age and stage appropriate manner. RSHE equips children and young people with accurate information, positive values and the skills to enjoy healthy, safe and positive relationships, to celebrate their sexuality and to take responsibility for their health and wellbeing both now and in the future. We recognise the importance of RSHE in preparing children and young people to live safe, fulfilled and healthy lives. The overarching objective of RSHE is to support children and young people through a journey of physical, emotional and moral development via the teaching of essential knowledge, skills and values within the framework of the law and provisions of the Equality Act, 2010. Our school’s vision for RSHE is linked to our whole school vision:
To Know: To know how to keep ourselves safe, happy and healthy
To Love: To love ourselves and each other and respect differences
To Share: To understand our responsibilities for looking after ourselves and others
Effective RSHE can make a significant contribution to the development of personal skills needed by pupils to establish and maintain relationships. RSHE will ensure children and young people are encouraged to understand the importance of stable, loving relationships, respect, love, and care. It also enables young people to make responsible and informed decisions about their health and wellbeing.
The RSHE programme at ASSR is spiral curriculum that enables pupils to build on their prior learning by revisiting some themes to further develop knowledge, values and skills in an age and stage-appropriate manner. As such, some themes are repeated to enable a deeper exploration of the related issues. The following themes will be covered in each year group:
If you require further information about the content of RSE including a copy of the RSE policy and scheme of work please contact our school office. You are also welcome to view the materials used should you wish to do so.
Whilst we believe that our programme at ASSR is very sensitive, parents do have the right to withdraw their child from aspects of the RSE curriculum. Please contact the school office if you would like to discuss this with the Head of School.

Attendance
https://www.gov.uk/school-attendance-absence
Our school target for attendance is 95%
Lateness
Punctuality is important educationally so that children don’t miss out on their learning time and is also a legal requirement. ASSR operates a soft start with our gates open from 8.30 and gates are closed at 8.50am. This is in order to ensure your child attends school on time in the mornings. If you are having problems getting your child to school on time, please make an appointment to see the class teacher to discuss how school can support you further.
Withdrawal from learning applications
Forms to request an absence from learning are available from the office, and at the bottom of this webpage.
We are not able to authorise time away from school unless there are exceptional circumstances and we require 14 days’ notice of any absence.
Some examples of exceptional circumstances:
Funeral of parent, grandparent or sibling
Holidays in term time
Family holidays are not covered by ‘exceptional circumstances’. ASSR will not authorise any term time holidays.
If a family chooses to take leave during term time for a holiday which is unauthorised they may receive a fixed penalty notice (£60 per parent, per child which increases to £120 if not paid within 21 days).
All schools have a legal duty to publish its absence figures to parents and to promote attendance. Equally, parents have a duty to make sure that their children attend. School staff are committed to working with parents as the best way to ensure as high a level of attendance as possible, and we thank you all for your support in this matter.

Our School Day
A typical day at All Saints' and St Richard's:
08:30 - The gate opens and children make their way to their classroom
08:50 - Morning registration
09:00 - Morning session begins
10:00 - Whole school worship
10:30 - Mid-morning session starts
13:00 - Afternoon registration and afternoon session starts
14:20 - EYFS and KS1 afternoon break
15:20 – End of the day and children are collected from the playground
(Total hours provided per week - 32.5 hours)
We are lucky to have our school in a beautiful rural setting. This brings many opportunities, however, a challenge it provides is parking at both the start and end of the school day. To limit this, we have a staggered start (your child can arrive anytime between 8.30-8.50) which greatly reduces congestion and parking issues.
We ask all parents to park sensibly to safeguard the children and families within our community and enable all to enter and exit the school safely.

The Friends of ASSR (PTFA)
The Friends is a group of people who volunteer together for the common good of the school. We organise fundraising events to raise money for the school to assist in purchasing extras for the school or put on non profit events for the benefit of the children at the school. Sometimes the group is referred to as the PTFA, the acronym stands for Parent Teacher Friends Association.
An update from The Friends
It's an exciting new school year and the PTFA is looking forward to putting together events for the children and parents to enjoy. The PTFA has recently held the AGM where details of all the fundraising from last year was discussed; the biggest fund raiser was the Summer Fair and the biggest expenditure has been the pond platform for forest school and £3000 towards the school's new trim trail. The minutes from the AGM can be found here.
Thank you to everyone who has helped out with PTFA events, we are always looking for volunteers and new suggestions and ideas. We love seeing parents and the school coming together for events that will benefit the children.
Dates for the Diary
Fundraisers and donations
Your daily shopping turned into every day magic! Easyfundraising partners with over 7,000 brands who will donate part of what you spend to our school. It won't cost you any extra, the cost is covered by the brand. Start your shop from the Easyfundraising page to benefit our school.
Our 50/50 club is a brilliant way to support the school as well as being in for the chance of winning a cash prize! Entry is £24 for a year, with 50% of the funds going to the school and 50% making up the prize money. Please contact the School Office if you wish to join the club or have any questions.
Donate your unwanted textiles in our clothing bank. By donating good quality, reusable items you will help save the planet and raise funds for our school. Clothing, shoes, soft toys and curtains, they all help! Anyone can donate, the bin is accessible at the front of school. Click here for a list of items that we can and can't accept.

School Meals
Children are offered a range of tasty and healthy school meals that are prepared freshly, on site every day by Chartwells. Lunch consists of a main meal (hot and cold with vegetarian options), pudding and water or milk. School meals are booked and paid for via ParentPay.
School meals are free of charge to all Infant children (from Reception to Year 2, inclusive). For more information on Universal Infant Free School Meals (UIFSM) please view the Government webpage.
View the new Spring Summer 2026 menu here
For children with food intolerances and allergies, Chartwells have a dedicated team of medical dietnutritionists on hand to support allergen aware children and their parents. More information on theirmedical diet process can be found here.
Parents and guardians can contact the medical diet nutrition team directly on: chartwells.medicaldiets@compass-group.co.uk
To find out more about Chartwells, visit their Love School Meals website or contact the school cateringteam.
Free School Meals
Your child may be entitled to Free School Meals (FSM) if you as parents receive one or more qualifying benefits. It is vital that all parents / carers who are entitled to these benefits apply for FSM even in Years R, 1 and 2 when you do not pay for school meals. If you do qualify, the school will receive extra funding to support your child’s learning in school.
You can apply for Free School Meals via this link.
Please refer to our Pupil Premium page for information about how this additional funding has been spent to help your children.
Fruit and Milk
EYFS and KS1 children benefit from the national free fruit and vegetables scheme and are provided with this on a daily basis to eat at break time. KS2 children are encouraged to bring in a healthy fruit or veg snack for morning break.
Early Years children are also entitled to a free serving of milk up until their fifth birthday, which parents need to sign up to, via Cool Milk.
Kindly note that we ask for packed lunches and snacks to be nut and pineapple free due to pupils having anaphylactic allergies.

Gold polo shirt with/without school logo.
Grey trousers / grey shorts / grey pinafore dress / grey skirt / green checked dress.
Black school shoes (not trainers).
Black, grey, white or bottle green socks/tights (no leggings).
Hair should be neat and tidy and worn with no extremes of style or colour.
Book bag for EYFS/KS1
Bottle green PE t-shirt with/without school logo
Black shorts / black joggers
Black jumper / black zipped top (plain or with school logo)
Please ensure all items of uniform, including drinks bottles (which should only contain water), lunch boxes and bags are clearly labelled – this allows quick return of all lost items.
If you need any help at all in relation to uniform, please contact the school office and we will be more than happy to help you.
